title: Project profile
description: What discovery concluded about a repository, per CONTEXT_SPEC 5. Two properties carry the meaning of this document. First, every field is a finding with a file behind it, so `signals` records the evidence and the aggregated fields are only ever as trustworthy as it. Second, `unrecognised` is the honest answer: a project that matches nothing yields `unrecognised: true` rather than a plausible-looking guess, because a confidently wrong stack is worse than an absent one. The typed Rust struct is TASK-030; this schema describes the shape the specification commits to, so the two cannot drift silently.

languages.description: Languages found, from manifests rather than file extensions.

frameworks.description: Frameworks inferred from dependency graphs, not from the presence of a directory name.

package_manager.description: Derived from lockfiles: `cargo`, `npm`, `pnpm`, `yarn`, `poetry`, `go`, `maven`, `gradle`. Null when no lockfile was found.

vcs.description: Version control in use. Null when there is no `.git`; a repository not under version control is worth saying plainly.

cloud_hints.description: Cloud providers implied by directory layout, e.g. `aws`. A hint, never a credential or an account.

confidence.description: Reported per signal; the profile-level value is the weakest of them, so one doubtful signal cannot be averaged away.

unrecognised.description: True when nothing was detected at all. `init` reports this instead of inventing a stack.

signals.description: The evidence behind the fields above: one entry per detected fact, naming the file that implied it. Optional, because a profile persisted for comparison does not have to re-carry it.

kind.description: The profile field this populates, using the spec's own names.

evidence.description: Project-relative path with `/` separators, so evidence compares the same on every platform.
